_source: Seed passages are the ones Christian traditions broadly cite for each theme -- creedal and canonical rather than distinctive to any one confession. Stamp ids are from ontology/interest-taxonomy.json as actually used in out/stamps-leveled.jsonl.
_intent: Doug, 2026-09-15: 'we need to take the major themes that christians agree on and put them to the test - we have a great start with the stamps'. This is the register those tests run against. Each theme names what is claimed, the passages that are agreed, and the stamp vocabulary that ought to find it.
_demoted: THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT THE REGISTER. Doug, minutes after it was drafted: 'but now I am thinking we let Paul, Jesus, Hebrews, John tell us what those themes are first and then go back looking for the evidence.' The list below was written from a creedal summary -- defensible, and not derived from this corpus. The register proper is the 21-id `themes` lane in interest-taxonomy.json, which covers 98% of sections and was derived FROM the text; see tools/themespine.py. What this file is still good for is its four `no_vocabulary` entries, which are holes the derived register cannot show because a vocabulary cannot report the words it lacks.
_what_the_test_found: tools/themespine.py --check, 2026-09-15. The 18 places the New Testament summarises itself were matched against the themes their sections carry, controlled against an NT-only baseline. `law_wisdom` is enriched 2.35x (9 of 18 against an expected 3.8) -- when the NT stops to summarise, it summarises the Law. `judgment` runs the other way at 0.61x despite being 55% of the corpus: the most narrated theme in the canon and the least summarised. n=18, so only law_wisdom clears noise.
_method: Harvest wide, verify every one, publish only what survived. Established by tools/declaredtypes.py on 2026-09-15: the strongest possible signal -- the New Testament's own typology vocabulary -- returned 30 verses of which only 12 were typology. A finder is not a verdict.
_ecumenical_note: 'Agreed' means agreed THAT the theme is in the text and central, not agreed about its dogmatic content. Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant readers differ sharply on how atonement works and what sanctification consists of; all three hold that the text teaches both. The register deliberately stops at that line. Where a theme's content is genuinely contested (justification, predestination, the mode and efficacy of baptism, ecclesial authority) it is not in this list, and adding one later means recording whose reading it follows.

_status_values.untested: no test has been run against it
_status_values.findable: the stamps recall the seed passages
_status_values.no_vocabulary: the taxonomy has no id for it -- a measured hole
_status_values.too_broad: a stamp exists but is carried by so much of the corpus that it selects nothing

themes.name: Creation
themes.claim: God made all that exists, freely, and called it good.

themes.name: The image of God
themes.claim: Humanity is made in God's image, and that grounds human worth.

themes.name: The Fall
themes.claim: Sin entered the world, and death through sin, and all have sinned.

themes.name: Covenant
themes.claim: God binds himself to a people by promise, and the promise holds.

themes.name: Deliverance from bondage
themes.claim: God hears affliction and brings his people out; the Exodus is the pattern.

themes.name: Law and commandment
themes.claim: God gives instruction for life with him and with neighbour.

themes.name: Sin and judgement
themes.claim: God judges evil, and the judge of all the earth does right.

themes.name: Grace
themes.claim: God's favour is given, not earned; he is merciful and gracious, slow to anger.
themes.note: Established 2026-09-15 building tools/giftresponse.py: the taxonomy has no `grace`, and the hinge pattern had to be detected on Greek lemmas instead. One of the most agreed themes in Christianity and the register cannot name it.

themes.name: Atonement
themes.claim: Christ died for our sins; by his wounds we are healed.

themes.name: Incarnation
themes.claim: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.

themes.name: Resurrection
themes.claim: Christ is raised, and the dead will be raised.

themes.name: Repentance and forgiveness
themes.claim: Turn, and be forgiven; God does not despise a broken heart.

themes.name: Faith
themes.claim: The righteous shall live by faith; Abraham believed, and it was counted to him.
themes.note: `promise_faithfulness` is GOD's faithfulness to his promise, which is a different claim from human trust. Using it here would be the `character_roles` error again -- a nearby id standing in for a missing one.

themes.name: The Holy Spirit
themes.claim: God's Spirit creates, empowers, indwells, and bears fruit.

themes.name: The people of God
themes.claim: God calls a people for himself: a chosen race, a royal priesthood.

themes.name: The kingdom of God
themes.claim: God reigns, the kingdom has come near, and it will come in full.

themes.name: New life and sanctification
themes.claim: What God does to a person is what makes the new life possible: a new heart, a new creation, a workmanship.
themes.note: This is the theme tools/giftresponse.py detects as the BRIDGE -- the middle term between the gift and the response. The seeds are Doug's own instances from 2026-09-15.

themes.name: Love of God and neighbour
themes.claim: Love the Lord your God, and your neighbour as yourself; on these hang all the Law and the Prophets.
themes.note: Jesus names this the greatest commandment and the taxonomy has no id for it at section level.

themes.name: Mission to the nations
themes.claim: In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed; go and make disciples of all nations.

themes.name: Hope and the new creation
themes.claim: Behold, I make all things new; creation itself will be set free.

themes.name: Worship and prayer
themes.claim: God dwells with his people and is to be worshipped in spirit and in truth.

themes.name: Suffering and perseverance
themes.claim: Affliction is real, God is present in it, and endurance produces character.

themes.name: Justice and the poor
themes.claim: Do justice, love mercy; defend the fatherless, the widow and the stranger.
themes.note: `stranger_sojourner` is a character role, not the ethical demand. If the test recalls the seeds only through it, that is a hole and not a hit.

themes.name: The word of God
themes.claim: God speaks; his word does not return empty and endures forever.
